questions.explanation: Fifty out of one hundred is half. Half of ten is five; half of eighty is forty.

questions.prompt: You share 80 oranges equally among ten baskets. Each basket has eight. What is 10% of the oranges?
questions.explanation: Ten percent is one tenth. One of the ten equal baskets contains eight oranges.

questions.prompt: Of the same 80 oranges, 10% is eight and 5% is four. How many oranges is 15%?
questions.explanation: Fifteen percent is ten percent plus five percent of the same starting amount. Eight plus four is twelve.

title: What does a percentage mean? Start with 100 squares
practice: For more mental arithmetic, try a round of Math Rush.

sections.html:
Imagine a tray with 100 little squares. Colour in 50 of them. You have coloured half the tray.

You can say “50 out of 100”, or write 50%. The symbol % means “percent”. Fifty percent means fifty out of every hundred: half.

Colour in 25 squares instead and you have coloured one quarter of the tray. That is 25%. Colour all one hundred squares and you have 100%: the whole tray.
sections.title: Percent means “out of one hundred”

sections.html:
A percentage describes a share, not a fixed number of objects.

Half of 10 oranges is 5 oranges. Half of 80 oranges is 40 oranges. Both are 50% of the oranges you started with, even though the number of oranges is different.

So whenever you see a percentage, ask: a share of what? In our next examples, we will always start with 80 oranges.
sections.title: The tray does not have to contain 100 things

sections.html:
On a tray of 100 squares, 10 coloured squares take up one of ten equal groups. That is why 10% means one tenth.

  1. Imagine sorting our 80 oranges into ten equal baskets.
  2. Each basket holds 8 oranges. Ten baskets of eight make eighty.
  3. One basket is one tenth of all the oranges. So 10% of 80 is 8.

In maths, sharing equally is called division. The sign ÷ means “divide”. You can write the basket step as 80 ÷ 10 = 8.
sections.title: Find 10% by making ten equal groups

sections.html:
Fifteen percent is ten percent and another five percent. Keep using the same original 80 oranges.

  1. We already found 10%: that is 8 oranges.
  2. Five is half of ten, so 5% is half as much. Half of eight is 4 oranges.
  3. Add the two shares: eight oranges and four oranges make 12 oranges.

So 15% of 80 is 12. We built the answer from two smaller, easier pieces.
sections.title: How do we find 15%?

sections.html:
We saw that 25% is one quarter. To find 25% of our 80 oranges, split them into four equal baskets.

Each basket holds 20 oranges. So 25% of 80 is 20.

If there are 20 oranges, how many is 50%?

Fifty percent means half. Split 20 oranges into two equal groups. Each group has 10 oranges.
sections.title: One quarter is another useful starting point

description: Percentages are a way to describe a part of something. Start with shaded squares, then use halves and small equal groups to make sense of the numbers.
